purpose: Deliver a finite open v1.2 product release that provides bounded minimum-quality coverage across the material human-AI collaboration lifecycle, is actually installable and usable on Codex, preserves dynamic native-first capability and carrier adaptation, fills only evidenced residual gaps, survives controlled historical and adversarial counterexamples, and is reproducible and releasable with explicit human authority. The current shortfall corpus is a requirements and counterexample source rather than a feature backlog; coverage permits sufficient native or external reuse and honest degradation, escalation, stop or claim limitation instead of requiring a bespoke Harness mechanism or static perfect score. Natural-task burden reduction, broad real-world effectiveness, distinct-Agent equivalence, and untested operating-system behavior remain continuing field-validation claims rather than release-completion prerequisites. v0.2 remains an immutable bounded calibration milestone, while v1.0 and v1.1 remain immutable stopped zero-outcome attempts; none can satisfy this program by inheritance.

increments.observedProblem: O1 requires one non-duplicative disposition for every fixed SG-01 through SG-12 source slice with controlled evidence for each claimed effect. The exact validator and observed-native-minimum environment manifest now strictly precede registration, and the named human has accepted the applicability, accountable-domain boundary and bounded claim ceiling, but no immutable task registration or measured result exists.
increments.hypothesis: One immutable pre-measurement registration can bind the accepted twelve-slice mapping, exact source custody, environment, validator, safety floors and claim exclusions before any controlled execution; after a separate activation commit, the same task-specific validator can exercise and independently replay all twelve observable verifier effects without installing a plugin, invoking a model, manufacturing natural demand or creating a generic evidence runtime.
increments.falsifier: Registration is post-hoc, does not bind the exact accepted mapping or environment, reclassifies a slice, permits implementation or prose as proof, executes a scenario before the registration binding is valid, fails any controlled effect or independent replay, promotes controlled evidence into comparative burden, broad effectiveness, distinct-Agent or untested-platform claims, requires a new ungranted side effect, or leaves task-created residue.
increments.stopCondition: The immutable registration strictly precedes measurement; all twelve registered controlled scenarios and independent replay pass under the exact validator and environment binding; the named human accepts the bounded O1 result; O1 is verified without expanding its claim ceiling; the increment closes and all task-created temporary resources are absent.

deliverables: content-addressed twelve-slice observation and independently replayed evidence

increments.observedProblem: O2 has a corrected exact package grant, an authenticated clean isolated Codex home, four committed controlled goals, a source-bound user-configured unavailable stop, an earlier task-specific validator and projection builder, and an exact code-owned private-resource disposition. The control repair materially changed the capture identity, so the observed-native-minimum manifest must be refreshed and an immutable registration must pass before any package installation or scenario execution.
increments.hypothesis: A refreshed committed starting manifest followed by one immutable O2 registration can bind the exact Codex version, environment, package digest, four scenario contracts, source-bound unavailable stop, human authority, cleanup lifecycle, earlier validator and projection builder. After a separate activation commit, installing only that package into the isolated home and running the four ordinary goal-level scenarios should demonstrate bounded Codex application, authority stop/resume, recovery, removal and zero residue without touching current user configuration.
increments.falsifier: The manifest or package identity drifts; installation or model execution occurs before a valid immutable registration; a scenario requires Skill, plugin or command syntax from the user; the simple native route gains unnecessary ceremony; the protected deletion occurs before a new exact grant; user configuration or existing credentials are copied or read; rollback or cleanup is incomplete; private locators or events enter public evidence; the validator changes after registration; or the controlled result is promoted beyond the tested Windows Codex suite.
increments.stopCondition: The refreshed manifest and immutable registration strictly precede installation and execution; the exact package is observed installed and active only in the authorized isolated environment; all four registered scenarios pass the earlier validator, including a separately granted protected deletion; the exact plugin, marketplace and isolated resources are removed; no repository or external task residue remains; the named human accepts the bounded O2 result; O2 verifies and the increment exits the current graph.

deliverables: four-scenario public-safe Codex observation and bounded O2 evidence

increments.observedProblem: The first immutable O2 attempt retained no credit after the legacy workspace-write route rejected the first nontrivial task-root write. The second immutable attempt resolved Codex 0.147.0 and the official built-in :workspace profile without legacy sandbox composition, passed the fixed 32-cycle four-worker allow-deny pressure probe, and installed the exact registered package only in the fresh isolated environment. The suite stopped before the authority and recovery scenarios, the exact plugin, marketplace, task roots and isolated resource were removed, and the retained public-safe counterevidence carries no O2 credit.
increments.hypothesis: The immutable second-generation O2 registration binds the official built-in :workspace profile without legacy sandbox composition, the exact Codex version, isolated starting state, package bytes, four ordinary goal-level scenario contracts, source-bound user-configured stop, prior validator and projection builder, separate protected-deletion gate, public-safe evidence projection and exact cleanup lifecycle.
